title: Ops Lab: Task Simulator and Safety Rails for Admin Utilities
creator: Leah Ramos
description: Build a lightweight 'Ops Lab' simulator that turns existing runbooks-as-tasks into sandboxed, replayable task graphs for training, QA, and step-by-step validation. The simulator should let engineers and support run runbook tasks in a controlled environment with injected fixtures (mocked infra APIs, canned KV cache, and fake GPU slots) and enforce safety rails (permission checks, dry-run gating, and automated rollback hooks). Goal is to reduce human error during oncall/playbook execution and surface gaps in runbook automation before live runs.
acceptance_criteria: A sandbox mode exists that can instantiate a runbook-as-task graph from an existing task definition and run it against mocked service endpoints (S3, leader-election, scheduler) without touching prod resources.
Safety rails implemented: role-based gating for destructive steps, explicit dry-run toggle, and an automatic abort on any high-severity simulated failure.
Simulator emits a step-level trace compatible with existing Console tracing and creates a replayable artifact (JSON) that can be attached to Linear tickets and PRs.
Integration tests cover at least three common admin utilities (scale-pool, cache-clear, model-fallback) demonstrating simulated success, failure, and rollback paths.
Documentation and a short tutorial notebook in Drive linked from the Console are published and reviewed by Support and SRE.
Performance: simulator can run a typical 12-step runbook in under 10s in sandbox mode on CI with mocked latencies configured.
Security sign-off recorded (KMS/credentials not used in sandbox; secrets sanitized in artifacts).
tasks: Design mock API layer and fixtures for core infra dependencies (storage, control-plane, scheduler)
Extend runbooks-as-tasks interpreter to support a 'sandbox' execution context and dry-run hooks
Implement permission/role checks and a reversible 'destructive' marker for steps
Wire simulator traces to Console tracing API and add export endpoint for replay artifacts
Create CI smoke tests with three representative runbooks and add to ops-tooling pipeline
Write tutorial doc and a short walkthrough notebook for Support and new SRE hires
Run a 1-hour validation session with Support, capture feedback, iterate on safety rails

notes: Trade-offs discussed: full hardware emulation is out of scope for MVP; we will instead rely on service-level mocking + latency injection to approximate behavior.
Decision: reuse existing runbook DSL with a thin adapter layer instead of forking interpreter to minimize divergence and maintenance cost.
